To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a "bootstrappable" IBFHE and attribute-based IBFHE scheme and characterize presently-known leveled schemes.

- We construct a "pure" identity-based fully homorphic encryption scheme from indistinguishable obfuscation, - We extend the result to an attribute-based setting, - We identify a class of leveled IBFHE that are not bootstrapped, and - We present a compiler from a leveled IBHE scheme to a pure IBFHE scheme.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: 1) the first "pure" IB/FHE scheme from ind. obf. with homomorphically-composable ciphertexts; 2) a compiler from a leveled IB/FHE scheme to a fully bootstrappable scheme; and 3) sufficient conditions for the existence of a compiler.
the design, implementation, and analysis of bootstrappable identity-based fully homorphic encryption schemes, as well as attribute-based fully homomorphic schemes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the problem of building bootstrappable identity-based fully homomorphically encrypted schemes remains open, and the present work represents progress toward that goal.
a bootstrappable fully homomorphic IBFHE scheme exists, but is not presently known to exist.
the problem of building bootstrappable IB-FHE is now solved, and that the remaining challenge is to develop a compiler from the leveled scheme to a boot-strappable scheme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have constructed the first "pure" IB-FHE scheme, and that we have characterized presently-known IB-FHE schemes in a way that would be helpful to develop a "compiler" for them.
we present the first "pure" IBHE scheme from ind. obf. and the first "pure", bootstrappable, leveled IBHE schemes, and provide sufficient conditions for bootstrapping IBHE schemes.
we have developed the foundations for bootstrapping in an identity-based setting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the "compiler" approach does not work, and a new approach is needed to achieve bootstrappable IB-FHE schemes.

the problem of bootstrapping in an identity-based setting is not fundamentally different from the problem in a public-key setting, and that a compiler from a leveled scheme to a bootstappable scheme is possible.
bootstrapping is a necessary ingredient for constructing a "pure" identity-based fully homomorphically-encrypted scheme, and that the problem of constructing a "pure'' scheme remains open.
